recipes.name: Stuffed Green Peppers
ingredients_raw: 1 (14.5 ounce) can whole peeled tomatoes, chopped

steps.text: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Cut the tops off bell peppers and remove the seeds. Cook bell peppers in boiling water for 5 minutes; drain. Sprinkle salt inside each bell pepper and set aside.
Place ground beef and onion in a large skillet over medium heat; cook and stir until beef is browned, about 5 minutes.
Drain off excess fat and season with salt and pepper. Stir in tomatoes, 1/2 cup water, rice, and Worcestershire sauce.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer until rice is tender, about 15 minutes.
Remove from heat and stir in cheese.
Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Stuff each bell pepper with beef and rice mixture; arrange open-side up in a baking dish.
Combine tomato soup with just enough water in a medium bowl to make the soup a gravy consistency.
Pour over the bell peppers and cover with aluminum foil.
Bake in the preheated oven until heated through and cheese is melted and bubbly, about 25 to 30 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Stuffed Green Peppers
raw_recipe.description: These stuffed green peppers with ground beef, rice, and Cheddar cheese take just 30 minutes to bake in the oven for a delicious weeknight meal.

review.reviewBody:
I didn't give it 5 stars 'cause I made changes based on others' suggestions that I felt improved the recipe. I halved the peppers (lengthwise), sauted onions separately along with 2 minced garlic pieces, cooked the rice separately, used 1 can of DICED tomatoes* (why would you ever buy a can of tomatoes and THEN dice them?), and mixed the ingredients together after browning the beef**, allowing them to warm slightly in the skillet before stuffing into the peppers. You can use the extra juice from the can of tomatoes to keep the rice from burning. I also added quite a bit of basil, oregano, and Italian seasoning, as well as extra Worcestershire sauce. Putting just a little cheese in the bottom of each pepper helped as well. Lastly, I only used one can of tomato soup. Even cut in half, 25 min was needed to get them nice & hot. Next time, I'll try adding some pepper as well.
* Using a can of diced tomatoes with jalepeno peppers adds just the right amount of kick to these! **You can also use 1/2 beef & 1/2 3-7% lean ground turkey to reduce fat content...tastes the same!

It was easy to put together. It takes a bit of time but is worth every minute. I browned the ground beef & onions on the stove top in my crockpot liner (by GreenLife) & then put it in the base on medium heat for 3 hrs. I used jasmine rice & canned diced roasted tomatoes. Added powdered garlic & smoked paprika to add depth to the flavor. Topped it with shreded chihuahua cheese. Turned out really tasty !!

I used 1 1/2 lbs of lean ground beef, browned that slightly then added 1 medium chopped onion, fried the onion w/the beef. added a spash of worchestershire. Removed a little over 8oz of the meet onion mixture to make 2 peppers for myself as I cannot have rice (keto) did NOT salt the meat mixture. added the chopped tomatoes & one box of Earthly Grains Long Grain & Wild Rice Mix Garlic & Herb (Aldi's)and 2 cups of water. Simmered w/a lid till rice was tender (20 mins?) Let that cool a lil and added the 1 cup of cheese. added 1/3 cup of cheese to my keto meat. Filled 6 peppers w/the rice meat mixture, divide mine w/no rice to 2 peppers. Instead of tomato soup, I used Food Lion hot chunky salsa on all (we like spicey food & there's sugar in the tomato soup, CARB! When baked till hot, I added shredded parm to the top & baked 5 mins more. Delicious! I gave 4 stars bcuz of my adaptations......I usually use Rice a Roni Spanish rice but find couldn't it!

I've done this recipe a few times, and I like it. I've had my way with it, though: now that I'm a diabetic, I substitute cooked barley for white rice. I also tried swapping in half a pound of Italian sausage meat for half a pound of beef. Finally, I cook it in the oven without the tomato soup (I pour it on top like gravy when serving time comes). It always comes up aces!

Fantastic! I diced the tops of the green pepper and added them to the meat/onions along with a jalapeño pepper. I substituted the tomato paste for the soup and added some basil and oregano. Additionally, I used a can of diced tomatoes for the whole tomatoes since that’s what I had in my pantry. For a final touch, I put a thinly sliced tomato on top to prevent the cheese from sticking to the foil. GREAT presentation!!

I added one clove of garlic to mixture. Used 1/2 pound of hamburger and 1/2 pound of chorizo. Used beef broth in place of water. I had only enough mixture to stuff 3 large peppers. Spread 1/3 of soup in bottom of casserole and spooned the remainder over the tops of the peppers. This a great recipe.

Absolutely delicious and well ballanced, but I did make some changes, and additions because of comments I read.

I bought diced canned tomatoes instead of whole tomatoes
I used a TBS of Worcestershire sauce instead of tsp
I added 1.5 TBS of diced, canned jalepeneo peppers, it was enough to give it a building spice that didn't overpower the dish.

I took the green pepper around the stem that I cut off and diced it and sautéed it with the onion. I also mixed the soup right away with the tomato’s rice and water instead of pouring it over the top. I also added chili powder, garlic salt, and onion powder to add some taste.

The recipe is so yummy. The only changes I made was to turn it into a casserole and I only used 1 medium bell pepper. I chopped and sauted the bell pepper and the onion with the ground beef and then followed the rest of the recipe. I poured the cooked ingredients into a sprayed casserole dish and added more cheddar cheese to the top. I then baked it for 20-30 minutes until the the cheese was bubbly and started to brown. (350 degrees) I will be making this regularly. My picky-eater husband loved it!

Generally, this is a tasty recipe with a an adjustment or two, or three. As has been suggested, I would add an extra tsp of Worcestershire to the meat mixture. I used Rao’s Tomato Basil Soup instead of a regular can of tomato soup. I poured it directly from the jar over the peppers without diluting. I added extra cheddar cheese on top of the peppers and then baked. I would suggest playing with the baking time. 30 minutes at 350 degrees didn’t seem long enough.

I made this by using around 1 1/3 pounds of meat. 3/4 ground burger, 1/4 hot pork sausage and 1/3 pound of chorizo. Oooo Laaa Laaa!! I cooked my onion and garlic with the meat and drained well. I halved a mixture of multicolored and green peppers - cooked my jasmine rice separately in beef broth - added just a bit of sharp cheddar cheese on the inside of the peppers, then put in the filling, then put cheddar and Parmesan on top. Cheddar was in the filling as well. I used double Worcestershire, oregano, basil and Italian seasonings. Nom nom!
I used a partial box of cream of tomato soup in place of the canned soup. Good, easy recipe. Made twice already.
Great. Recipe made enough to stuff four huge peppers. Next time, I will double the Worcestershire and also cut the peppers in half before stuffing.

We love this recipe and we keep it simple and make mostly per the recipe given. We just use diced can tom and don't cook the peppers in water. We like the peppers more crisp and it tastes excellent! We make this often.
yes instead of using beef i used ground chicken instead
Love it and it’s simple
I make this all the time and it's always a hit. I also freeze a couple as it makes a great last minute emergency meal. If still frozen just cook a little longer.
Love this recipe. Husband calls it a keeper.
I used fresh garden green peppers and fresh tomatoes from my garden.
I had left over cooked rice so I added it to the browned burger & added chopped grn pepper. Used maranara instead of tomato soup.
